occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records: Seven out of eight staff files evaluated were observed to be missing A Pre-Employment Affidavit for Applicants for Employment at Certain Child Care Operations (Form 2912). One out of eight staff files evaluated were missing a statement signed and dated by the employee showing he has received a copy of the child-care center's operational and personnel policies.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records (26 TAC §746.901)

occurrences.finding: AP Initial background checks submitted - At the time you hire someone: The governing body and director were observed at the operation without a background check. This was corrected when they both left the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Initial background checks submitted - At the time you hire someone (26 TAC §745.621(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: it was observed that trash was present on the playground area accessible to children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: Three out of eight staff files evaluated were observed to be missing trainings for emergency preparedness, preventing and controlling the spread of communicable diseases, including immunizations, administering medication, preventing and responding to emergencies due to food or an allergic reaction, understanding building and physical premises safety, and handling, storing, and disposing of hazardous materials
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current: Two student were observed to need updated immunizations in their files.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current (26 TAC §746.613(b))

occurrences.finding: Access to Personnel Records: One staff members file was not available for evaluation during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Access to Personnel Records (26 TAC §746.909)

occurrences.finding: Reduction of child/caregiver naptime ratio by 50% allowed, If 13 or more children in care, children are 18 mo. or older and other standards met: The operation had reduced the number of caregivers in the naptime ratio in a room with infants present.    This was corrected when a caregiver came back from break and was added to the room's ratio.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Reduction of child/caregiver naptime ratio by 50% allowed, If 13 or more children in care, children are 18 mo. or older and other standards met (26 TAC §746.1613(a))

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age: A 15 month was present in a room with a child who was three years old.    This was corrected when the director ensured that the classes were reorganized in a manner that separated the 15 month old while still maintaining ratio.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age (26 TAC §746.1605(1))

occurrences.finding: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes: The operation did not have up to date fire drills.    This was corrected when a fire drill was conducted while CCR was present.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §746.5205(1))

occurrences.finding: Inspect Fire Extinguishers Monthly: The monthly  fire extinguisher inspections were not up to date.    This was corrected when the director checked the fire extinguishers while CCR was present.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Inspect Fire Extinguishers Monthly (26 TAC §746.5307(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Children's Product Certification: The operation's Childrens Product Certificaton form was not up to date.    This was corrected when the director updated the form while CCR was present.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Children's Product Certification (26 TAC §746.801(18))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two: An infant between the ages of 12-17 months was observed watching tv in a high chair.    This was corrected when the administrative assistant in charge of the operation removed the infant from the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two (26 TAC §746.2207(a))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times: Children were observed watching t.v. while eating breakfast.    The children were just finishing up eating when I walked in. This was corrected when the caregiver said she would turn the t.v. off if any other children came in to eat.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(4))

occurrences.finding: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device: There was sufficient evidence to support the claim that an infant was allowed to sleep in a bouncer.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2426(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Activities for Infants - Not in Restrictive Device for more than 15 Minutes: There was sufficient evidence to support the claim that that infants are left in restrictive devices for more that 15 minutes at a time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Activities for Infants - Not in Restrictive Device for more than 15 Minutes (26 TAC §746.2417(2)(B))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: There is sufficient evidence to support the claim that a caregiver was using a personal electronic device while supervising infants.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries: There was sufficient evidence to support the claim that parents were not notified by the operation of less serious injuries.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries (26 TAC §746.307(c))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: There was sufficient evidence to suggest that a child was not being properly supervised when placed in a stroller alone in a room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: There was sufficient evidence to suggest that a caregiver was using a personal electronic device while caring for children during naptime.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep: There was sufficient evidence to suggest that a child was forced to sleep during naptime.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep (26 TAC §746.2905(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Restrictive device for time out: There is sufficient evidence to suggest that a child was placed in a restrictive device for an extended period of time in order to curb undesired behavior.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Restrictive device for time out (26 TAC §746.2805(8))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: There was sufficient evidence to suggest that caregivers repeatedly grabbed, pulled, and pushed a child in order to keep him restrained in a stroller for an extended period of time in order to correct undesired behavior.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: There was sufficient evidence to prove that an employee used poor judgment, resulting in the injury of a child in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: There was sufficient evidence to prove that hot food was left accessible to a child, resulting in an injury.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Safe and Sanitary: There is sufficient evidence to prove that a caregiver prepared and distributed food in an unsafe manner, resulting in an injury to a child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Safe and Sanitary (26 TAC §746.3317)

occurrences.finding: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness: There was sufficient evidence to prove that the operation did not report one child and two caregivers contracting COVID to licensing.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness (26 TAC §746.305(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Communicable Diseases: There was sufficient evidence to prove that the operation did not record one child and two caregivers contracting COVID on the Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form 7239 or other similar form.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Communicable Diseases (26 TAC §746.701(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Infant Feeding Instructions: There was sufficient evidence to prove that infant feeding instructions were not being maintained. Two of three infant feeding records reviewed show infants without infant feeding instructions signed and updated in the last 30 days.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Infant Feeding Instructions (26 TAC §746.801(2))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: Four children did not have up to date immunization records.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Storage of Medication - Refrigerate Separate from Food: A bottle of generic Pepto-Bismol was being stored in a refrigerator with food items.    This was corrected when the acting director removed the bottle and placed it in storage.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Storage of Medication - Refrigerate Separate from Food (26 TAC §746.3807(3))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Conducted by Fire Marshal: The operation did not have proof of a fire marshall's inspection within the last 12 months.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Conducted by Fire Marshal (26 TAC §746.5101(b))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Medical Authorization: Two children did not have complete Emergency Medical Authorization Records.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Special Needs Statement (26 TAC §746.605(12))

occurrences.finding: Report Number of Employees: A review of the Employees Who Left Employment in 2021 data from February 23, 2022, revealed that the center had not reported the number of employees who left employment in 2021 by February 22, 2022, as required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Employees' Attendance: Based on the information obtained, it is determined that there is evidence to support that the operation do not keep an attendance record for the director and assistant director.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Employees' Attendance (26 TAC §746.801(5))

occurrences.finding: Director Presence Routine During Operating Hours: Based on the information obtained, it is determined that there is evidence to support that the operation director is not routinely present.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Presence Routine During Operating Hours (26 TAC §746.1011)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver did not display good judgement when a child was tied up in a blanket during nap time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep: A caregiver attempted to force a child to lay down and sleep by tying the child up in a blanket.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep (26 TAC §746.2905(1))
